archetype.name: Underachiever (lineup-driven)
archetype.definition: A year after a 90-win playoff team, Seattle kept an A-graded rotation but fell to 76-86 because the offense sank to 28th in runs and the defense graded worst in the league.

report.headline: An A rotation couldn't carry a bottom-three offense and the league's worst defense.

recap.finish: 76-86, third in the AL West, five games behind 81-81 Houston; missed the postseason
recap.body:
This was a pitching-and-park team that stopped scoring. Seattle's starters earned an A, and run prevention finished 16th, about where it sat a year ago. The lineup fell from 9th in runs per game in 2025 to 28th, and team OPS dropped from .740 to .693. Over the season the Mariners scored 664 and allowed 722. The -58 differential fits a 76-86 team, and the +1.2 W vs Run Diff says close games neither saved nor sank them. They were about as bad as their record.

The season had two halves. Through June they were 44-43 and had outscored opponents by 13 runs, with May (15-13, +23) the best month. Then it came apart. July went 9-15 on 87 runs scored, and August went 11-16 while allowing 169 runs in 27 games, more than six a night. August's -74 differential is larger than the full-season deficit, so outside that month Seattle was a plus-16 team. A 12-12 September with 126 runs scored, the best scoring month of the year, came too late. They closed 6-4 in the last 10.

The offense rested on two bats. Randy Arozarena was an All-Star, with a 151 wRC+, a .381 OBP, 26 homers and 26 steals, worth 5.5 WAR, more than double anyone else on the roster. Dominic Canzone added a 134 wRC+ at DH. Most of the rest hovered near league average once the park is accounted for. Julio Rodríguez posted a 104 wRC+ with a .307 OBP. Josh Naylor slugged .350 over 650 PA and was worth 0.5 WAR. Cal Raleigh hit .182. Taylor Ward got on base at .359 but slugged .311. A lineup with that many league-average regulars, in an 85 park factor, produces raw run totals near the bottom of the league. That is where Seattle finished.

The defense made things worse. Fielding Runs came in at -48, last in the league, continuing a slide from -10.5 in 2024 and -29.6 in 2025. J.P. Crawford was -10 at short, and four other regulars were at -4.6 or worse. The effect shows in the pitchers' gaps between ERA and FIP. Bryan Woo had a 3.24 FIP and a 4.01 ERA, George Kirby 3.90 against 4.33, and closer Andrés Muñoz 3.34 against 4.24. The staff pitched better than its 4.20 ERA, 19th in the league, suggests. The fielders behind it gave runs back.

The Mariners finished five games behind a .500 Houston team in a division no one ran away with. That makes the margin frustrating. The 44-43 first half was on pace to stay in the race, and a merely bad August instead of a disastrous one would have kept them close. This was the franchise's first losing record in the five-plus seasons the sheet covers.

highlights.title: Arozarena carried the lineup alone
highlights.body: Arozarena had a 151 wRC+ and 5.5 WAR, ranking 9th of 182 outfielders, with a .381 OBP and a 26/26 season. He was the only hitter above 2.8 WAR, which explains why one star could not lift a D-graded group. His production came from on-base skill and power together, which makes it more repeatable than a batting-average spike.

highlights.title: Five starters, real depth, A grade
highlights.body: Gilbert, Kirby, Woo, Hancock and Miller each started at least 22 games and combined for about 791 innings. That durability earned the rotation an A. Woo was the best of them by the underlying numbers, with a 3.24 FIP and 4.1 WAR. Gilbert struck out 205 with a 1.09 WHIP. The starting pitching is the part of this roster that already works.

highlights.title: Canzone a legitimate second bat
highlights.body: Canzone's 134 wRC+ with 23 homers ranked 6th of 36 designated hitters. He was the only regular besides Arozarena who clearly beat league average. His .484 slugging matched Arozarena's, and that power is the kind of production this lineup needs more of.

lowlights.title: Offense fell from 9th to 28th
lowlights.body: Runs per game dropped from 9th in 2025 to 28th, and OPS fell to .693. Naylor's .350 slugging, Raleigh's .182 average and Ward's .311 slugging took three lineup spots out of the power game. The 85 park factor depresses raw totals, but wRC+ adjusts for it, and most of the lineup still sat near 100. That points to a shortage of above-average bats, not just a tough park.

lowlights.title: League-worst defense, three years sliding
lowlights.body: Fielding Runs of -48 ranked last of 30, and the number has worsened each year since 2023's +14.8. Crawford's -10 at shortstop led the problem. The ERA-over-FIP gaps for Woo, Kirby and Muñoz show the cost landing on the pitchers. A trend this long reflects the roster's makeup, not bad luck.

lowlights.title: The August collapse
lowlights.body: Seattle allowed 169 runs in August against 95 scored and went 11-16. That -74 differential is larger than the full-season deficit. In the other months the staff allowed about 4.1 runs a game. The sheet doesn't show the cause, but a single month that far out of line looks more like a bad stretch than the team's true level.

arc.note: Seattle was a 44-43 team with a positive run differential through June. It then went 20-31 across July and August, with August's 169 runs allowed doing the most damage. A 12-12 September stopped the slide but could not make up the ground.

recap.nextYear: The record was earned. A +1.2 W vs Run Diff means there is little bad luck to expect back, so improvement has to come from the roster. The rotation is the foundation: an A grade, five starters with real innings, and Woo's 3.24 FIP suggesting he is better than his 4.01 ERA. The bullpen's C grade hides a closer in Muñoz whose 37.1% strikeout rate and 3.34 FIP point to a better ERA ahead. Bazardo (-0.5 WAR, 4.73 FIP) and Domínguez (11.9% walk rate) are less convincing. The real work is the lineup and the defense. Arozarena and Canzone are the only clearly above-average bats, Naylor and Raleigh need rebounds, and a -48 Fielding Runs team will keep turning good pitching into ordinary run prevention. Raley's 60-day IL status is another unknown. If the August run prevention returns to the level of the other months and two more hitters reach a 110 wRC+, this is close to the division's 81-win bar. Without that, it repeats this season.

confidence.note: Full 162-game season; record matches the run differential.
